caption: The drawing consists of two detailed, grayscale renderings of a spoon, presented horizontally with the bowls on the left side and the handles on the right. The upper spoon is shown with the front side visible, with the engraved letters "N.A.P." on the end of the handle. The lower spoon is depicted with the back side visible, where a rectangular maker’s mark or inscription is present near the end of the handle. Both spoons feature a smooth, slightly rounded bowl and a handle that widens and flattens towards the end. Below the two primary drawings is a boxed, smaller-scale technical diagram, which provides dimensions and outlines for the spoon, displaying both a side view and a top view with corresponding measurements: 9 3/4 inches in total length, 3 3/4 inches for the bowl, and 2 1/4 inches for the width of the handle end. The artist's signature "G. Winter" and the scale notation "1/4" = 1'" appear near the bottom right corner of the page. The composition is monochromatic, rendered in shades of gray on a lightly tinted background, and all elements are contained within a simple rectangular border.
title: Silver Spoon
